handoff: Approve: all six criteria met, each with a test that asserts it (light route in all four workflow copies, resolution input, review routing, anchors); 2 minor notes, 0 blocking; test/typecheck/emits green.

findings.title: 'keeps the PR body' is proven only by routing
findings.detail:
AC5 says 'open-pr pushes and keeps the PR body without running describe'. The test proves that approve goes to open-pr without describe. It does not show open-pr leaving the body alone; that follows from open-pr reading the unchanged pr.md. The slice's S3 (an end-to-end walk on real git) is still open, as the handoff says.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Cover it in the S3 end-to-end walk if a later slice adds one.

findings.title: A resolver fix after a resolution review sends the story down the full path
findings.detail:
On changes_requested, resolve fixes the resolution with an ordinary commit and goes to update. Because that commit is not a merge, the next update ends done, so the story runs the full test → qa/review → describe path rather than a second short resolution review. That is safe, but it costs more than the light path promises. The handoff's Notes already raise it.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: A later slice or round could have the resolver amend the merge instead, or route the re-entry back to the resolution test.
